goals.en:
Upon the successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
- Understand the physical basis of climate change and Arctic amplification
- Distinguish drivers, impacts, and tipping points related to climate change
- Recognize feedbacks and the complexity of the spatial and temporal scales involved
- Distinguish the consequences of climate change for nature and people
- Develop a critical attitude to climate mitigation and adaptation
- Communicate complex problems in a clear and artistic way

description.en:
The changing climate is one of the biggest threats to development and impacts the most vulnerable people and ecosystems on the planet. Anthropogenic drivers are undoubtedly causing this climate change. This offers a potential for mitigation by our society. But the accelerating and diversifying impacts of climate change have also made clear that adaptation strategies are needed too.

While temperatures have been rising globally, the effect of climate change is most intensely experienced in the Arctic, a phenomenon called Arctic amplification. That is why this course focuses on the Arctic, where various tipping points have been identified and wide-ranging changes, adaptations, and uncertainties have been researched and documented.

What is happening in the Arctic will also affect the rest of the world. Well-documented examples are sea-level rise due to melting ice caps and the polar vortex causing extreme weather events.

This course aims to develop your knowledge of drivers of climate change and the impact of climate change as well as to explore why we should engage in mitigation and adaptation. It will provide you with a knowledge base to take responsibility for our planet.

The course has a link with all of the Sustainable Development Goals as they will all be affected by climate change if we don’t take action. More specifically, the course will have a special emphasis on SDG 13: Climate Action and SDG 15: Life on land and also link to SDG6: Clean water.

This course is part of the Earth and Environment track in the major Energy, Ecology and Climate. The course provides a theoretical basis and detailed insights for discussing climate change. It will build on the foundation course The Earth System and connect to other courses of the Earth and Environment track, namely:
Ecosystem Processes (100)
Data for Future Energy and Climate (200)
Climate Data and Services (300)
